status: FROZEN before any training, request or scoring; approved by the owner on 2026-10-16 (with the Jev arms)
role: the MASSIVE robustness run of docs/reviews/round3/synthesis.md section 6 (priority 2): do the confirmatory MASSIVE findings survive other held-out-domain draws, and does a deployable version of the 'rows' effect exist?

findings_under_test.F1: the specialist's lead over Gemma on MASSIVE (+4.4 weighted points, not significant; +6.1 without general quirky, post hoc)
findings_under_test.F2: Gemma rejects few held-out-domain requests without out-of-scope rows (23%; 5% of play)
findings_under_test.F3: labelled out-of-scope rows in the retrieval pool raise Gemma's rejection (23 to 91%, +13.3 weighted), but those rows came from the same domains as the test out-of-scope turns
findings_under_test.F4: an explicit scope instruction was never tried on MASSIVE

status_of_results: SENSITIVITY ANALYSIS, not confirmatory: MASSIVE has no unused in-scope test items left, so the new draws reuse test utterances that earlier runs used (as in-scope or out-of-scope turns under other label sets). Results are reported as such and never pooled with the confirmatory family.

draws.rule: for k = 0, 1, 2, ...: numpy default_rng(20261018 + k).choice(eligible, 6, replace=False), eligible = the 16 MASSIVE domains other than general and qa; the first three are the test out-of-scope domains (T), the last three the rows-source domains (R); a draw is skipped if T equals the confirmatory draw {email, iot, play} or an earlier T. The first three accepted draws are used. Computed while writing this file (design only, no scoring):
draws.label_set: the labels of the 12 domains in neither T nor R; both T and R are out of scope for every system in that draw

items_per_draw.in_scope: 1,000 test utterances of the kept domains, drawn with the draw's seed
items_per_draw.out_of_scope: 250 test utterances of the T domains, drawn with the draw's seed
items_per_draw.text: normalised as in confirmatory_protocol.json (lower-case, punctuation other than apostrophes removed)
items_per_draw.unit: single turns (no sessions); the endpoint is turn-level
items_per_draw.frozen: artifacts/massive-robustness/items.json, SHA-256 88e6051264a41e8a19782cb16331aec27642076c76714c3fcb36e65b4f06611c (each draw: 1,000 in-scope / 250 out-of-scope; train 7,532 / 6,704 / 7,745 rows; dev 400 / 100; rows 250 + 250)

systems.specialist: 150M Ettin encoder retrained per draw on the kept domains' training rows (normalised), learning rate 2e-4, 6 epochs, seeds 20261007, 20261015, 20261016; temperature on 400 kept-domain dev items; dev-selected detector with the prior-weighted threshold using 100 dev items of the T domains (the same asymmetry as the confirmatory run, stated)
systems.jev-1.13.0: optional, the same arms through Jev's interface (TypeSafe key)
systems.prompt: the workflow_massive zero-shot system prompt with the draw's labels; user message with 20 BM25 neighbours as in the confirmatory run

pool_arms.no_rows: kept-domain training rows only (the confirmatory primary condition)
pool_arms.same_source_rows: plus 250 training rows of the T domains with the out-of-scope code (as run C: rows from the domains that are tested)
pool_arms.cross_source_rows: plus 250 training rows of the R domains with the out-of-scope code (deployment-realistic: examples of some unsupported requests, not of the future ones)
pool_arms.instruction: no_rows pool, with the run D instruction sentence adapted to the skill list added to the system prompt (Gemma and Qwen)

original_draw_arm: the instruction arm for Gemma and Qwen on the 1,216 confirmatory MASSIVE turns (email, iot, play held out), paired with runs A and B; no rows arms here because the original label set has no second held-out source

hypotheses.M1_specialist_vs_gemma: per draw, specialist minus Gemma (no rows) in weighted turn accuracy; two-sided weighted sign-flip clustered by intent; reported per draw and as the count of draws with the confirmatory sign (+); no Holm claim (sensitivity)
hypotheses.M2_gemma_rejection: Gemma's held-out rejection without rows per draw and per T domain (descriptive)
hypotheses.M3_same_source_rows: Gemma and Qwen, same_source_rows minus no_rows, weighted accuracy, one-sided; 3 draws x 2 models, Holm
hypotheses.M4_cross_source_rows: Gemma and Qwen, cross_source_rows minus no_rows, held-out rejection and weighted accuracy, one-sided; 3 draws x 2 models = 6 tests on weighted accuracy, Holm. This is the main question of the run.
hypotheses.M5_instruction: Gemma and Qwen, instruction minus no_rows, weighted accuracy, one-sided; on the original draw (2 tests) and on the 3 new draws (6 tests), Holm over 8
hypotheses.also_reported: in-scope kept, held-out rejected and intent accuracy for every arm; the post hoc signal-detection c and d' per arm

outcome_sentences.M1 same sign in 3 of 3: On three further held-out-domain draws the specialist stays ahead of Gemma on MASSIVE ({values}).
outcome_sentences.M1 mixed: On further held-out-domain draws the specialist-minus-Gemma difference on MASSIVE changes sign ({values}): the confirmatory MASSIVE result depends on which domains are held out.
outcome_sentences.M4 significant: Labelled examples of unrelated unsupported domains raise the general model's accuracy by {d} points: out-of-scope examples help beyond the domains they come from.
outcome_sentences.M4 not significant: Labelled examples of other unsupported domains do not help; the +13-point rows effect of the confirmatory run required examples of the very domains being tested.
outcome_sentences.M5 significant: One scope sentence raises the general model's accuracy on MASSIVE by {d} points.
outcome_sentences.M5 not significant: A scope sentence does not repair the general model's acceptance of sibling-domain requests on MASSIVE.

cost.basis: measured per-turn cost on the confirmatory MASSIVE turns: Gemma 0.094e-3, Qwen 0.139e-3 USD; rows arms have the same prompt length
cost.per_draw: 1,250 items x (Gemma 4 arms + Qwen 4 arms) = 10,000 calls, about 1.17 USD
cost.jev_optional: about 15,000 requests, roughly 0.5 to 1.5 USD on the TypeSafe key
cost.gpu: 9 specialist trainings (3 draws x 3 seeds), about 1-2 minutes each; one GPU job at a time
cost.budget: spent before 68.36 of the 80 USD cap; remaining after this run about 7.8

code: src/bakeoff/massive_robustness.py (stages build, train, check, hosted <model>, jev_check, jev, analyze); runner scripts/run_massive_robustness.sh
limits: Items reuse MASSIVE test utterances (sensitivity, not confirmatory). Three draws of three domains each; play is a test domain in two draws and a rows source in one. 250 out-of-scope items per draw give wide intervals on rejection by domain.
jev: jev-1.13.0 through Jev's interface (jev_rerun_protocol.json conventions): retrieval state with label names; rows labelled 'out of scope' in the state; the instruction arm appends the scope instruction to Jev's scope question; scope at probability 0.5; included at the owner's request (2026-10-16)
execution: one process per general model and one for Jev, in parallel (different hosts); each process has its own cap (3 USD) and the total stays below run_cap_usd by the estimate; spend reconciled from saved rows afterwards
instruction_text: The labelled examples show only supported skills. A message that resembles them but asks for something none of the skills covers is out of scope: answer scope: no. (added to the first line of the system prompt)
tests_note: M3-M5 one-sided p-values are half the two-sided sign-flip p in the predicted direction (symmetric null); Holm within each family over the general models; Jev reported beside them, outside the families
